In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying T cell clonal expansion, activation and anergy in vivo.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that regulate the immune response.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of T cell activation and tolerance in vivo.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
clonal expansion of T cells is a normal and integral part of the process leading to anergy and death.
SEB induces a specific T‐cell‐mediated immunological response that is characterized by clonal expansion, followed by clonal deletion and clonal anergy.
the clonal expansion, followed by the anergy of Vβ8 T cells is not a direct consequence of TCR stimulation, but rather a consequence of the activation of accessory cell populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
clonal expansion is not sufficient for anergy and that anergy is not sufficient for cell death.
the clonal expansion, followed by anergy and death, are the three stages of a T cell immune response to a superantigen.
the immune response to SEB in vivo is characterized by an early phase of clonal expansion followed by a late phase of anergy, which in turn is followed by cell death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune response to superantigens is very complex and that the response to superantigen is not just a simple activation or tolerance response.
clonal expansion precedes both anergy and death.
the immune system is not just capable of expanding clones, but it also can delete them.
